newsitem.title: THAILAND: PTTEP says proved reserves at 502 mmboe.
newsitem.headline: PTTEP says proved reserves at 502 mmboe.

text.p: PTT Exploration and Production Plc said its remaining proved reserves of all projects as of December 31, 1996, stood at 502 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe), a company statement said on Saturday.
The amount has increased by four percent, or 17.9 mmboe, from the amount reported as of June 1996. The major portion is gas which accounted for about 91 percent of the reserves.

In the period between July 1-December 31 last year, PTTEP and its subsidiaries achieved total production of 7.3 mmboe of gas and crude, the statement said. Production was running at an average rate of 40,000 barrels per day (bpd).

The growth of remaining proved reserves resulted mainly from the increase of reserves in PTTEP's joint ventures, especially in Burma's Gulf of Martaban where gas reserves increased to 6.4 trillion cubic feet from 5.7 trillion.

Probable and possible reserves of all projects totalled 527.7 mmboe, down by 342.7 mmboe from the last report on June 30, 1996. The decline resulted from some of the probable and possible reserves being converted into proved reserves, the statement said.
Proved reserves are the volume of petroleum that geological and engineering data indicate with reasonable certainty to be recoverable under existing economic, technical and political conditions.
